I have been farming sorghum here in the North West for many years, and our soils are tired, so I will buy a few bags of fertilizer from the agro-dealer to give the crop a boost on this 1.36 hectare plot. I will sow the local sorghum seed I saved from last season because it is what I know and trust, and those improved seeds are too expensive for me this year. My family and I will put in most of the work, but I will hire some young men from the village for about a month to help with the planting and weeding when the rains start. We have no irrigation here, and sorghum does not need spraying like cowpea, so I will not use pesticides or water the plot.
